_README: Visa-free-but-K-ETA-required guide: Kazakhstan → Korea. Visa-free 30 days (max 60 within any 180-day period), but Kazakhstan is NOT on the temporary K-ETA exemption list, so K-ETA must be applied for. Numbers grounded in facts.json (visa-kazakhstan-free, keta-fee-validity).

verdict.headline: No tourist visa needed — but you must apply for K-ETA.
verdict.sub: Kazakhstani passports are visa-free for short tourism (up to 30 days, and no more than 60 days within any 180-day period). But Kazakhstan is not on the K-ETA waiver list, so you must get a K-ETA before you fly. With a valid K-ETA you're then exempt from the e-Arrival Card.
verdict.stay: Up to 30 days (max 60 within any 180-day period)

highlights.title: No visa for up to 30 days
highlights.body: Under the Korea–Kazakhstan visa-waiver agreement, Kazakhstani passport holders enter Korea visa-free for short-term tourism for up to 30 days per visit — capped at 60 days within any 180-day period. There is no tourist-visa application to file.

highlights.title: But you DO need K-ETA
highlights.body: Kazakhstan is not among the 22 countries/regions on the temporary K-ETA waiver, so you must apply for K-ETA before boarding. It costs KRW 10,000 (about US$8), is valid for 3 years with multiple entries, and is applied for only at the official site k-eta.go.kr.

highlights.title: K-ETA replaces the e-Arrival Card
highlights.body: Once you hold a valid K-ETA you're exempt from the e-Arrival Card — you don't file both. (If you're exempt from K-ETA by age — 17 and under or 65 and over — file the free e-Arrival Card instead.)

tldr: No tourist visa — Kazakhstani passports are visa-free for up to 30 days (max 60 within any 180-day period).

Apply at least 72 hours before departure; a valid K-ETA then exempts you from the e-Arrival Card.
Bring a passport valid for your stay plus proof of onward/return travel.

items.title: Confirm you're visa-free
items.detail: Kazakhstani passports enter Korea visa-free for short tourism (up to 30 days, max 60 within any 180-day period) — there's no tourist visa to apply for.

items.title: Apply for K-ETA (required)
items.detail: Apply at the official site k-eta.go.kr at least 72 hours before boarding. The fee is KRW 10,000, valid 3 years with multiple entries. Beware copycat sites that charge extra — only k-eta.go.kr is official.

items.title: Check passport & onward ticket
items.detail: Make sure your passport is valid for your stay, and have a return/onward ticket plus your first accommodation address.

items.title: At immigration
items.detail: With a valid K-ETA you don't file the e-Arrival Card. Show your passport at arrival; fingerprints and a photo may be taken. Keep it tourism — no paid work on visa-free entry.

items.q: Do Kazakhstani passport holders need a visa for Korea?
items.a: No — for short-term tourism, Kazakhstani passport holders enter Korea visa-free and can stay up to 30 days. You do not apply for any tourist visa.
Up to 30 days per visit, and no more than 60 days within any 180-day period. For a longer stay you'd need the appropriate visa.
Yes. Kazakhstan is not on the temporary K-ETA waiver list, so you must apply for K-ETA before boarding — at the official site k-eta.go.kr.

items.q: How much is K-ETA and how long is it valid?
items.a: It costs KRW 10,000 (about US$8), is valid for 3 years, and allows multiple entries. Apply only at k-eta.go.kr.

items.q: Do I also need the e-Arrival Card?
items.a: No — if you hold a valid K-ETA you're exempt from the e-Arrival Card. You file one or the other, not both.

items.q: Can I work or study on this entry?
items.a: No. Visa-free entry is for tourism and short visits only; working or studying requires the appropriate visa.
